mstts:express-as.prosody:
As we wrap up, let's take a moment to really sit with what this journey means. The path of antiracism isn’t something you finish, or walk alone. It’s a lifelong practice—one that asks for honesty, courage, and compassion, both for yourself and the people around you. Here’s what you can carry forward:
Notice that white supremacy operates as a system—it's bigger than any one person’s bias. Take an honest look at the beliefs you’ve taken in over time, and recognize where you might be complicit, even in small ways. It’s okay to feel discomfort, or even denial. Moving through those feelings builds real resilience and accountability. But don’t stop at awareness—turn what you know into action, both in your own life and within your community. Step up to challenge the systems and institutions that are at the root of inequality. And remember, keeping up the momentum means taking care of yourself, leaning on others for support, and pausing to celebrate every bit of progress. You’ll make mistakes—that’s part of the process. Each one is a chance to repair, to learn, and to recommit. Most importantly, let antiracism become part of your everyday life, shaping a legacy that moves us all closer to justice and equity. This isn’t about perfection, or proving your worth. It’s about showing up, again and again, ready to see clearly, listen deeply, and act with real integrity. When you feel tired or uncertain, know that those feelings signal growth, not defeat. Every step you take—no matter how small—adds to a wider movement for justice. By tending to your own growth, supporting those around you, and engaging wholeheartedly, you create ripples that reach far beyond your own life. The journey is long, but you’re never walking it alone. With patience, persistence, and compassion, you can help build not just a better future for yourself, but a more just and loving world for everyone.
